entries.subject: ClientIP: check every proxy for trustiness (#2844)
entries.rationale: Unanimous. Parent validateHeader walks the XFF chain LEFT-to-right and unconditionally selects items[0] -- the client-supplied end -- so even with SetTrustedProxies correctly narrowed the attacker dictates ClientIP(). Both parties executed it: with RemoteAddr 40.40.40.40, SetTrustedProxies([40.40.40.40]) and 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 30.30.30.30', parent returns 1.2.3.4 and the commit returns 30.

The cited hunk merely swaps the priority of two equally client-supplied headers: parent read X-Real-Ip then X-Forwarded-For, commit reads X-Forwarded-For (LEFTMOST element, the most spoofable value of all) then X-Real-Ip. entries.rationale: Unanimous. entries.rationale: Unanimous. Parent ClientIP() returned Header.Get("X-Real-IP"), then X-Forwarded-For, then RemoteAddr, with zero peer validation -- any remote client could dictate the value. Dependency bump inside the cmd/protoc-gen-go-grpc submodule (grpc v1.79.3 -> v1.81.0) plus regenerated .pb.go version stamps. protoc-gen-go-grpc is a protoc plugin - it never runs a gRPC server, so the poc ('attacker sends crafted RPC requests to a gRPC server') describes nothing that exists here. Supply-chain hygiene for a build tool; reverting exposes no runtime path in this repo.

Client-side xDS HTTP filters are things like fault injection and gcp_authn - a client that skips its own filter simply fails to attach a token, it does not bypass any server-side control. Genuine memory-leak bug (interceptors leaked on in-place RDS updates because usableRouteConfiguration was overwritten in an atomic.Pointer without stopping the old one), but the trigger is the xDS management server pushing route updates, not client traffic. Genuine certificate-validation weakness. TLSInfo.ValidateAuthority looped over ALL of t.State.PeerCertificates and returned nil if ANY of them (intermediates, and whatever else the peer chose to send in the chain) passed VerifyHostname, so a per-RPC :authority override could be validated against a non-leaf cert. Now only PeerCertificates[0]. Release-noted as a bug fix; reverting restores the loose

Not a memory leak. The change adds r.Close() on error paths in rpc_util.go decompress() so mem.BufferSlice buffers go back to the sync.Pool instead of being reclaimed by the GC. Failing to return a pooled buffer costs allocation/GC pressure, never unbounded growth - 'until the system runs out of memory' is wrong. RELEASE NOTES: None; this is pool-reuse efficiency.

Real over-permissive authorization. Pre-fix authenticatedMatcher.match fell through from non-matching URI SANs to DNS SANs and then Subject DN, so a peer cert whose URI SAN should have been authoritative could still satisfy an ALLOW policy via its Subject DN. gRFC A41 requires first-non-empty-source-only. Maintainers state it 'allows an authorization bypass in certain scenarios'. Reverting restore

Primarily dead-code removal: UpdateAddresses is no longer reachable in the xDS LB tree after pick_first became the universal leaf policy, so it becomes a logging no-op and endpointInfo drops from atomic.Pointer to a plain pointer. The incidental leak fix (removing scw from the endpoint map on Shutdown) is bounded by EDS/resolver churn, not request traffic, and the claim's own severity is 'low'. RE

The only consequence of the old behaviour is that the CLIENT that advertised the tiny limit treats the oversized response headers as a protocol error and tears down its own connection. Correctness fix in brand-new internal code (ready_reader.go was added days earlier by #8964); its only non-test consumer is credentials/alts/internal/conn/record.go, which falls through to a blocking p.Conn.Read that does surface io.EOF. Impact is a client channel briefly not noticing a peer's graceful FIN - a normal peer action, not an attack, and no unbounded loop or leak. RELEASE NOTES: N/A.

Adds a spec-compliance validation that the sum of LbEndpoint weights in one locality stays <= MaxUint32, accumulating in a uint64 so no overflow happens even in the check. Input comes from the xDS control plane (trusted config source), and the consequence of the un-validated case is skewed weighted LB, not a crash. Validation hardening with no exploitable pre-existing state.

Resource-hygiene cleanup, not an exploitable leak. On the server side the parent already had `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(...); defer cancel()`, which tears down the DoHandshake stream regardless - Close() only does stream.CloseSend(), it does not release the handshake semaphore. The claim's premise is factually wrong: the 8KB limit is gated on GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_8KB_DEFAULT_HEADER_LIST_SIZE, which boolFromEnv defaults to FALSE. Default behaviour after this commit is still 16MB; the release note says it will flip in v1.82.0. Reverting changes nothing an operator sees by default. Opt-in future hardening.
